text:
I


Race of Abel, eat and sleep;

God smiles upon you with pleasure.


Race of Cain, in the mud

fall and die miserably.


Race of Abel, your sacrifice

smells sweet to the Seraph!


Race of Cain, will your torment

ever have an end?


Race of Abel, see your crops

and your flocks prosper;


Race of Cain, your entrails

howl hungry like a dog.


Race of Abel, warm your belly

beside the patriarchal fire;


Race of Cain, in your den,

poor jackal, tremble with cold!


Race of Abel, love and multiply!

Your gold also breeds children;


Race of Cain, fiery heart,

beware those appetites.


Race of Abel, you grow and fatten

like a bedbug in wood!


Race of Cain, along the roads,

lead your fearful people.


II


Ah, race of Abel, your carrion

will fertilize the steaming soil!


Race of Cain, your task

has not yet been fulfilled;


Race of Abel, see your disgrace:

the pike has conquered iron!


Race of Cain, rise to heaven,

and throw God down to earth!

translation.title: Abel and Cain
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish version of Baudelaire’s French original. Roman-numeral sections and the antiphonal pattern are retained.
